heuristic.applicability: Prefer when drawer is open, block pose is near demonstrated valid tunnel support, and the HL agent starts at 300:440 overlap or restarts at an observed intermediate phase with a TCP pose/configuration offset but no known collision/contact failure. The object must be visible and the local correction must remain reachable. This policy is not a recovery guarantee.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open/stable, block remains low in the tunnel, current TCP/configuration is finite and collision-free, gripper is open unless restarting after a plausible grasp, and two causal frames are available across a switch.
handoff.exit_conditions: Block and TCP show coupled motion under closed fingers, block has cleared world z 0.16 outside the tunnel, and local corrections have turned toward the drawer destination.
handoff.failure_signatures: Local increments drift away from object/destination, object does not follow a closed gripper, phase oscillates around closure/lift, block remains below clearance, or IK repeatedly fails/reaches limits.
handoff.overlap_role: All 300:840 actions are supervised; 300:440 teaches continuation from predecessor retreat/approach states and 680:840 teaches continuation into successor clearance/reorientation/transfer states.
handoff.successor_readiness: Switch when observed block/TCP coupling is stable, clearance is exceeded and the local motion points toward target_pose; the successor shares 680:840.

heuristic.limitations: Repeated local corrections can drift globally and a body delta is not invariant by construction to a large block displacement; the object-frame prior covers that case. It remains dependent on phase inference from only two frames and can be unsafe if contact/grasp status is misread; the destination-frame clearance-guarded prior is preferable when premature lateral transfer is the main risk. IK feasibility and collision freedom are not guaranteed. No contact truth or failed-grasp recovery appears in training.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Inputs are two causal frames emphasizing qpos/qvel, world TCP, object/TCP transform, object/destination transform, finger width and clearance. Learned actions are 7-D: translation in the fresh current TCP frame (metres), relative rotation vector (radians), and gripper scalar. encode_targets forms inverse(pre-action measured TCP) times commanded FK pose per slot. decode_action composes the represented displacement with the newly measured TCP for that slot and calls verified IK from newly measured qpos. Standard DiffusionBackbone and fixed temporal/numerical recipe remain unchanged.
heuristic.rationale: Entry at 300 begins with the same nominal TCP in the inspected demonstrations, so deployment handoffs can be more variable than training. The assigned segment itself spans very different intermediate TCP/configuration states: high approach at 420, low alignment at 520:540, closed-gripper pull at 560:600, lift at 640:700, and reorientation/transfer at 780:820. Expressing every target as a fresh measured-TCP body displacement makes the commanded correction locally invariant to an offset entry TCP and avoids replaying a fixed world waypoint. Two causal frames and explicit object/TCP, destination/object, finger and clearance relations condition which correction is appropriate; measured qpos/qvel preserve redundancy, limits and reachability. Benefit for unseen handoff offsets is expected, because all demonstrations are successful nominal trajectories.
heuristic.statement: Fresh-TCP body-delta prior: diffuse each Cartesian command as an SE(3) displacement from the measured TCP immediately before that executed slot (body-frame translation, rotation vector, gripper). Prefer it for valid mid-skill restarts or predecessor handoffs whose arm/TCP configuration differs from the demonstrations while the block remains near demonstrated tunnel support.

subgoal: With the drawer already open, move from the drawer-retreat state to the tunnel, descend within the tunnel clearance, align an open gripper around the block, close on it, pull it horizontally out of the tunnel, then lift it above the 0.16 m tunnel clearance and begin transfer toward the drawer. Approximate entry: drawer open and stable, block low near z=0.08, gripper open. Approximate exit: block held with closed fingers and elevated around z=0.30-0.32 or higher, outside the tunnel and moving toward the drawer.
